correctness.rationale: The original equations reduce on the invariant negative-opinion sector to p'= -beta p[y+(1-y)p] and tau*y'=tanh((1+kp*p+kx*y^2)y)-y. The scalar p'<=-beta*p^2 gives p->0. The zero-infection scalar y trajectory is a lower barrier for y and has y~(2ct/tau)^(-1/2); hence p decays at least exp(-a sqrt(t)). The limiting opinion drift is strictly negative at every fixed y>0 (atanh(y)>y+y^3/3 and kx<1/3), forcing y->0. A direct uniform Taylor expansion produces w=1/y^2 with w'=2c/tau-2d/(tau*w)-2kp*p*w/tau+O(p+w^-2). Since w=O(t), p*w is integrable, yielding w=(2c/tau)t-(d/c)log(t)+K+o(1). The opinion error from the leading t^-1/2 term and the infection term in (log p)' are integrable, giving a strictly positive stretched-exponential prefactor. The neutral-opinion SIS comparison is exact. Symbolic coefficients and finite-time diagnostic data were checked with the included verify.py; their finite scope is explicitly distinguished from proof.

value.rationale: At R0=1 the standard SIS neutral-opinion trajectory has a universal 1/t decay, while ANY strictly negative initial opinion in the same nonlinear opinion-coupled model leads to globally proven exp(-B sqrt(t)) decay with positive prefactor and B explicitly dependent on physical opinion timescale. This changes the asymptotic functional class and clarifies the impact of persistent, slowly relaxing risk aversion on critical disease clearance. The peer-feedback fifth-order term changes the sign of the first logarithmic correction at kx=2/15. The classification is natural to the originating epidemic model and cannot be inferred from its equilibrium table alone; relevance is limited to deterministic homogeneous criticality.
